reality.qualifier: Cars.com confirms the 2026 Long Range AWD delivered MSRP at $50,380, including $1,390 destination charge. (2025 Long Range AWD was previously $49,380 delivered.)
reality.verbatim_quote: Currently only available in Long-Range All-Wheel Drive form, the Model Y version now on sale is basically the Launch Series for $11,000 less; pricing starts at $50,380 (price includes $1,390 destination charge).

sources.name: Cars.com — 2026 Tesla Model Y Gets Long Range AWD Variant, Starts at $50,380

narrative_one_liner: 'Starting at $47,990' excludes the $1,390 destination fee — actual delivered MSRP is $49,380–$50,380.
narrative: The 'starting at' price quoted in marketing and configurator headlines excludes the mandatory $1,390 destination fee. The delivered MSRP a buyer encounters at order placement is $49,380 (2025) or $50,380 (2026 refresh). Edmunds also notes the Long Range AWD is not eligible for the federal Clean Vehicle Credit, which is sometimes referenced in advertised effective prices.
methodology_notes: Cars.com is a single Tier-2 source; this is industry-standard practice (most US auto manufacturers exclude destination from headline) so corroboration via additional sources is straightforward in Phase 1.
caveats: Industry convention: virtually all US auto-industry advertised MSRPs exclude destination. This deception is universal, not Tesla-specific.
FTC has issued guidance on 'all-in' pricing primarily targeting hotels and rentals, not autos.
alternative_explanations: Destination fee varies by ZIP code in some configurators; quoting it as a single number on a national page would be inaccurate. Listing it separately is defensible — but typography and salience suggest the headline is what buyers anchor on.
Tesla also runs price changes more frequently than typical OEMs; quoted numbers can be outdated within weeks.
